descriptionChirho: An Aramaic noun meaning 'lord' or 'master,' appearing in Daniel as both a form of personal address ('my lord,' with 1cs suffix) and in construct ('Lord of'). English glosses show 'my lord' and 'Lord of'; Spanish 'mi senor' and 'Senor de'; Hindi 'mere svami' (मेरे स्वामी) and 'prabhu' (प्रभु); Arabic 'sayyidi' (سَيِّدِي) and 'rabb' (رَبُّ); Korean 'na ui juyo' (나의주여) and 'juin' (주인); Swahili 'bwana wangu' and 'Bwana wa.' Both clusters denote the same concept of lordship/authority with different pronominal suffixes and syntactic frames.
